questions.prompt: State the magnetic force law for a moving charged particle.
questions.answer:
The magnetic force law is
\[
\vec F_B=q\vec v\times\vec B
\]

questions.prompt: State the magnitude of the magnetic force on a particle of charge magnitude \(|q|\).
questions.answer:
The magnitude is
\[
F_B=|q|vB\sin\theta
\]
where \(\theta\) is the angle between \(\vec v\) and \(\vec B\).

questions.prompt: When is the magnetic force on a moving charged particle zero?
questions.answer: It is zero if \(q=0\), \(v=0\), \(B=0\), or if \(\vec v\) is parallel or antiparallel to \(\vec B\), so \(\sin\theta=0\).

questions.prompt: A proton moves at \(3.0\times10^5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) perpendicular to \(0.20\,\mathrm{T}\). Find the magnetic force magnitude.
questions.answer:
For perpendicular motion,
\[
F_B=qvB=(1.60\times10^{-19})(3.0\times10^5)(0.20)=9.6\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm{N}
\]

questions.prompt: An electron moves at \(4.0\times10^6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) at \(30^\circ\) to a \(0.50\,\mathrm{T}\) field. Find the force magnitude.
A charge \(2.0\,\mu\mathrm{C}\) moves perpendicular to a magnetic field at \(1.5\times10^3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). The force is \(6.0\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{N}\). Find \(B\).
questions.answer:
For perpendicular motion,
\[
B=\frac{F_B}{|q|v}=\frac{6.0\times10^{-4}}{(2.0\times10^{-6})(1.5\times10^3)}=0.20\,\mathrm{T}
\]

questions.prompt: A positive charge moves east through a magnetic field pointing north. What is the force direction?
questions.answer: Use the right-hand rule for \(\vec v\times\vec B\): east crossed with north points upward. For a positive charge, the force is upward.

questions.prompt: An electron moves east through a magnetic field pointing north. What is the force direction?
questions.answer: For a positive charge, east crossed with north points upward. An electron is negative, so the force reverses and points downward.

questions.prompt: A particle moves through a magnetic field but its speed does not change. Why is this consistent with a nonzero magnetic force?
questions.answer:
The magnetic force is perpendicular to the velocity. It can change the direction of the velocity while doing no work:
\[
\vec F_B\cdot\vec v=0
\]

questions.prompt: A particle has velocity components parallel and perpendicular to \(\vec B\). Which component determines the magnetic force magnitude?
questions.answer:
Only the perpendicular component determines the magnitude:
\[
F_B=|q|v_{\perp}B
\]
The parallel component contributes no magnetic force.

questions.prompt: Find the perpendicular speed component for a particle moving at \(8.0\times10^4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) at \(60^\circ\) to \(\vec B\).
questions.answer:
The perpendicular component is
\[
v_\perp=v\sin\theta=(8.0\times10^4)\sin60^\circ=6.9\times10^4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]

questions.prompt: Show from the cross product why magnetic force is perpendicular to velocity.
questions.answer:
The magnetic force is
\[
\vec F_B=q\vec v\times\vec B
\]
A cross product is perpendicular to both input vectors. Therefore \(\vec F_B\perp\vec v\), so the force is perpendicular to the velocity.

questions.prompt: A particle of charge \(5.0\,\mathrm{nC}\) moves perpendicular to \(0.080\,\mathrm{T}\) and feels \(2.0\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm{N}\). Find its speed.
questions.answer:
For perpendicular motion,
\[
v=\frac{F_B}{|q|B}=\frac{2.0\times10^{-6}}{(5.0\times10^{-9})(0.080)}=5.0\times10^3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]

questions.prompt: A positive charge moves in the \(+x\) direction through a magnetic field in the \(+z\) direction. Find the force direction.
questions.answer: Use \(\hat x\times\hat z=-\hat y\). For a positive charge, the force points in the \(-y\) direction.

questions.prompt: What magnetic field direction would make a positive charge moving in \(+x\) feel force in \(+y\)?
questions.answer: We need \(\vec v\times\vec B=+\hat y\). Since \(\hat x\times\hat z=-\hat y\), choose \(\vec B\) in the \(-z\) direction because \(\hat x\times(-\hat z)=+\hat y\).

questions.prompt: Derive the tesla in base force-current-length units from the force on a wire.
questions.answer:
For a wire perpendicular to the field,
\[
F=ILB
\]
so
\[
B=\frac{F}{IL}
\]
Therefore
\[
1\,\mathrm{T}=1\,\mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-1}}
\]

questions.prompt: A charge moves at fixed speed through a region where \(\vec B\) is uniform. What happens to its kinetic energy if no other forces act?
questions.answer: Its kinetic energy remains constant. Magnetic force does no work because it is perpendicular to displacement at each instant.

questions.prompt: A charged particle experiences no magnetic force in a region. Does this prove \(B=0\)? Explain.
questions.answer: No. The particle might be stationary or moving parallel to the magnetic field. Since \(F_B=|q|vB\sin\theta\), zero force does not by itself prove \(B=0\).

questions.prompt: Two particles have equal speed and equal charge magnitude in the same magnetic field. One moves perpendicular to the field and one at \(30^\circ\). Compare force magnitudes.
questions.answer:
The perpendicular particle has
\[
F_\perp=|q|vB
\]
The \(30^\circ\) particle has
\[
F_{30}=|q|vB\sin30^\circ=0.5|q|vB
\]
So the perpendicular particle feels twice the force.

questions.prompt: Explain why the magnetic force law must include both a magnitude rule and a direction rule.
questions.answer: The magnitude rule \(F_B=|q|vB\sin\theta\) gives only the size of the force. Magnetic force is a vector, so the direction must also be determined by \(\vec v\times\vec B\) and by the sign of charge. Without the direction rule, the predicted path of the particle is incomplete.
